subject: FinTrust: request for vuln governance attestation and SLA timeline
messages:
From: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@auditpartners.io>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: security@fintrust.com
Date: Fri, 1 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: scan cadence & CVE remediation SLA for SOC2 evidence

Hi Sean,

We are kicking off the SOC 2 audit collection for FinTrust and need your vulnerability management evidence packet. Specifically we need:

- Current scan cadence (tools + weekly/monthly schedule)
- SLA commitments for CVE remediation by severity (Critical/High/Medium) and how exceptions are handled
- Recent scan output or a summary table for the last 30 days (CSV is fine)
- An attestation that the remediation ownership and rollback play is in place for critical fixes

Can you provide these items and indicate the named owners for triage/remediation? Auditor asks for a signed attestation or an email trail stamped by an engineering manager.

Thanks,
Claire Dunn
Senior Auditor, Audit Partners
claire.dunn@auditpartners.io

--
Attachment: audit_request_template.pdf (stub)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Claire Dunn <claire.dunn@auditpartners.io>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 1 Aug 2025 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: scan cadence & CVE remediation SLA for SOC2 evidence

Hi Claire — thanks for the heads up. We can provide a compact evidence packet by early next week. Summary below and I will attach the CSV and commit log in the follow-up.

Summary (high level):
- Scan cadence: weekly authenticated host and container scans (Tuesdays 0300 UTC), daily quick container image scans for new images, monthly external network vulnerability scan. Tools: internal agent (Redwood Agent v2.1) + third-party scanner (AegisScan v4.7) for external.
- SLA commitments: Critical (0–72 hours to mitigation plan + patch/rollback or compensating control), High (0–14 days to mitigation plan), Medium (30 days), Low (90 days)
- Exception/rollback: We have an approved rollback playbook for critical changes (document: rollback-playbook.pdf). If remediation requires customer-impacting change, we run a canary and 6-hour rollback window, with an on-call emergency rota.
- Ownership:
  - Critical triage & escalation: Hannah Schmitt (Security Ops Manager)
  - Remediation coordination & patch delivery: Monica Patel (Infrastructure Engineering)
  - Verification & proof-of-fix / scan re-run: Irene Choi (Vulnerability Engineer)

I will attach: scan-report-2025-07-31.csv and cve-commit-log-2025-08-04.xlsx.

Let me know if you want the rollback-playbook signed and I will include a stamped attestation.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0119

Attachments: scan-report-2025-07-31.csv (stub), cve-commit-log-2025-08-04.xlsx (stub)

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 2 Aug 2025 08:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: scan cadence & CVE remediation SLA for SOC2 evidence

Thanks Sean — noted. Quick ops notes for the packet:

- I will validate the 72-hour gating for Critical: that SLA covers time-to-mitigation-plan, not necessarily code-drop. We document the plan in the ticket and escalate to SEV when needed.
- For Critical CVEs affecting customer workloads we run the rollback playbook in the following sequence: triage -> emergency patch if safe -> canary rollout (1% traffic) -> full rollout OR immediate rollback if metrics degrade.
- Monica: can you confirm patch windows and the next scheduled maintenance (so auditors see when we would schedule a forced patch)?
- Irene: please include the re-scan proof column (scan-run-id + timestamp) in the cve-commit-log spreadsheet. That helps the SOC2 reviewer.

Hannah
Security Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
